vedic_reference.note: Kashyapa is a sage and progenitor in Hindu mythology. He is the father of many demigods including the Ashwini Kumaras and Dhananjaya, as well as the great sage Vedavyasa, the compiler of the Vedas and Mahabharata.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kashyapraj holds great significance in Indian culture, where it is revered as the name of a wise and learned sage. Kashyap is believed to have authored several important Hindu texts, such as the Atharv Veda and the Shiva Purana. He is also known as the father of the sage Ved Vyasa, who compiled the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kashyapraj carries a deep spiritual significance, representing the divine creator's role in our lives. According to Hindu beliefs, Kashyapraj embodies the creative force of the universe and is believed to bestow wisdom, knowledge, and understanding upon those who bear his name. The name is a constant reminder that we are all creations of the divine andq are meant to use our wisdom and knowledge to contribute positively to the world.

historical_references.reference: Rigveda 10.129 - Hymn to Prajapati, one of the primary deities in Hinduism. Kashyapraj is mentioned as the son of Prajapati and his wife Prasuti.

Mahabharata - One of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. Kashyapraj is mentioned as a sage and the father of various important figures in Hindu mythology, including the sage Vamana and the sage Agastya.
